stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This funding aims to enhance their co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, aligning with rising DoD interests in space security. The cash infusion underscores a growing appetite for defense-oriented space technologies.
stories.soWhat: When the DoD is throwing money at co-orbital security, you know the competition for space is heating up—literally.

stories.head: Space Force triples launch contract ceiling to $17B
stories.body: The Space Force has announced a tripling of its launch contract ceiling to $17 billion, reflecting increased demand for satellite launches and related services. This move comes as part of a broader strategy to bolster U.S. capabilities in space amid geopolitical tensions. Expect a flurry of activity as contractors scramble to get a piece of the pie.
stories.soWhat: When the Space Force opens the floodgates, it's not just about launches—it's a signal that they expect a lot more traffic in orbit.

stories.head: LegendSpace raises $29.5M to develop AI rocket engines
stories.body: Chinese startup LegendSpace has attracted $29.5 million in an angel funding round to expedite its AI-driven rocket engine development. The company aims to leverage algorithms to cut down on traditional engineering timelines, potentially reshaping the competitive landscape for rocket propulsion. This funding reflects a growing trend of using AI in aerospace engineering.
stories.soWhat: If AI can really cut down development times, traditional aerospace firms might need to rethink their decades-long playbook.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on the Space Force's next moves

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
